title: Black Bar Pierce — Korean Ink Editorial
description: A pure black-and-white editorial portfolio built around one typographic gesture: a thick black horizontal bar that Pretendard ExtraBold Korean letterforms visually pierce, splitting glyphs between white space and solid ink. No color, no ornament — the bar is the entire brand.
philosophy: This template is a single-gesture design: everything is subordinated to the black-bar pierce, a device borrowed from Seoul fashion editorial where heavy Korean type becomes sculptural object rather than mere label. It refuses accent color, decorative frames, gradients, and icons on principle — not from restraint but from conviction that the letterform at 150px already contains all the drama the slide needs. It is built for designers who understand that removing is harder than adding, and whose audience respects that discipline. The gray mono Latin subtitle exists only to anchor language and role; it defers completely to the Korean name above.
goodFor: Korean-language personal branding decks where the name itself is the logo
Print-ready PDF portfolios sent to editorial, fashion, or senior design clients
Single-discipline designers (product, UX, identity) needing a singular title-card presence
Closing slides and section dividers requiring maximum typographic impact with zero color
avoidFor: Chart-heavy UX case studies requiring color-coded data layers or annotated flows
Multi-contributor agency decks needing flexible accent colors per team or brand
Presentations projected in dim or low-contrast rooms where black-on-white bleeds out
Portfolios relying on full-bleed color photography as the primary compositional element
author: harness

examples.promptCore: One Korean display name is bisected by a full-bleed black horizontal bar that splits each glyph between open white above and solid ink below. The mood is cold Seoul editorial: stripped, authoritative, the name functioning as logo rather than label. Compositional rhythm is blade-cut stillness — generous white above the bar, the gray mono Latin line resting quietly beneath. Avoid softness, shadow, gradient, or icons; all drama belongs to the letterform colliding with the bar.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with roughly 8% outer margin; the Korean display name spans the full column width as a single centered line, positioned in the upper half of the slide. A thick horizontal bar bleeds edge-to-edge, intersecting the name at approximately mid-glyph height, splitting each letterform between white space above and reversed ink below. The gray mono Latin subtitle occupies a single narrow line directly beneath the bar, left-aligned to the name's left column edge. No header band, page number, or footer chrome appears on this slide.

examples.promptCore: The content slide repurposes the black bar as a grammar mark — a caesura between a pierced section header and the body below. Compositional rhythm is vertical and deliberate: heavy typographic mass bears down against the bar from above, while the body zone breathes with generous spacing and reduced visual weight. The feeling is Seoul editorial — ink-heavy, architectural, silences as intentional as the marks. No secondary rules, no tints, no icon-led bullets; the bar and the type are the only instruments.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with 8% outer margins left and right. The thick black horizontal bar repositions to mid-slide, acting as a structural divider between a compact Korean/Latin section-header zone above and a content body zone below — the pierce illusion is preserved on the section label rather than the hero name. Content items — project titles, role descriptors, or a single extended quote with attribution — occupy columns 2–11, anchored in the breathing zone beneath the bar. Hierarchy is achieved through size contrast alone: one dominant pierced label above, subordinate mono Latin body below; folio numeral isolated at bottom-right with no footer band.
